description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy across three metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—across a range of initial confidence values from approximately 0.71 to 1.00. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is scaled linearly with tick marks at intervals of 0.03, ranging from 0.71 to 1.00. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also linear, with values ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. The blue line with circular markers, representing Final Accuracy, starts at a value of approximately 0.88 when initial confidence is 0.71, decreases to around 0.75 at 0.73, then rises to a peak of about 0.92 at 0.79 before gradually declining to approximately 0.87 at 1.00. The green dashed line with circular markers, representing Initial Accuracy, begins at 0.55 and increases steadily to around 0.88 at 1.00. The orange dashed line with diamond markers, representing Δ Accuracy, starts at approximately 0.35, drops to 0.08 at 0.73, remains low until 0.82, then increases to a peak of about 0.28 at 0.83, declines to 0.1 at 0.86, and then fluctuates, peaking at 0.42 at 0.91 before decreasing to around 0.08 at 1.00. Error bars are present on all data points, indicating variability in the measurements.
